answer: A reputation trellis resists Sybil attacks: an agent earns trust only through verified work attested by distinct counterparties, so trust grows along real transaction paths. A newcomer spinning a fable of grand history with no attested work stays at the untrusted edge. Forging a convincing web costs real fees and time per fake identity, while an ivory-tower shortcut like a self-issued credential is ignored, since trust never flows from a single source. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents pay almost nothing.
